entities.name: Basilique Sainte-Clotilde de Reims
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Basilica of Sainte-Clotilde de Reims, dedicated to Saint Clotilde (also Clothilde, circa 474-545 CE) — the Frankish queen who converted her husband, Clovis I (King of the Franks), to Christianity in 496 CE, one of the most consequential religious conversions in European history — is a Catholic church in Reims, the city already famous as the coronation site of French kings and as the location of the magnificent Gothic Reims Cathedral. Clotilde's role in Clovis's baptism at Reims by Bishop Remigius links her directly to the founding religious act of the French nation.

Saint Clotilde's historical significance is extraordinary: as a Burgundian Christian princess who married the pagan Frankish king Clovis I, her persistent encouragement of her husband's conversion was pivotal in his decision to receive Christian baptism in Reims (traditionally dated to December 25, 496 CE, though scholars debate the exact date). Clovis's baptism had enormous consequences: it made the Frankish kingdom an ally of the Catholic Church against Arian Christianity (most other Germanic kingdoms were Arian), provided the ideological foundation for the later alliance between the French monarchy and the papacy, and began the process by which the Franks became the most powerful Catholic kingdom in Europe — ultimately leading to Charlemagne's 800 CE coronation as Holy Roman Emperor.

The Reims basilica honoring Clotilde stands in the city that witnessed the baptism she facilitated — making the dedication historically resonant. Reims Cathedral is the place where most French kings were subsequently anointed and crowned, continuing the religious legitimation tradition that Clotilde's influence on Clovis initiated. The basilica represents the Catholic Church's recognition of Clotilde's role in France's foundational religious transformation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of Sainte-Clotilde de Reims — honoring the queen whose conversion of Clovis I made the Franks Catholic and transformed European religious history, standing in the city whose sacred status she created — is historically meaningful as a monument to one of the most consequential royal conversions in Western history.
